LESSON: MICROORGANISMS

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: GENERAL SCIENCE
Strand: Life Science
Topic 1.7: Microorganisms
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 13

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Microorganisms, part of Life Science in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 GENERAL SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: How are micro- organisms important in day to day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify microorganisms that affect human beings,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Microorganisms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. explain modes of transmission of microorganisms in human beings,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Microorganisms in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Microorganisms together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: as the learner uses digital devices with assistive technology to research on infections caused by

microorganisms as well as their control and prevention mechanisms.

● Communication and collaboration: as the learner discusses and shares information gathered during group discussion on

types of microorganism infections, control and prevention.

Values:
Respect is promoted as the learner listens to others’ opinion while discussing methods of controlling and preventing

microorganism infections.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

Socio Economic and environmental issues - Poverty eradication; as the learner sensitises the community on the

significance of food preservation and the economic importance of microorganisms.

Suggested Learning Resources:

● Print textbooks in appropriate font and colour,

● Braille textbooks,

• Digital devices with assistive technology such as screen readers and screen magnifiers.

Key Skills:

Describing methods of control and prevention of infections caused by microorganisms.
